subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: Should the browser login handoff ship as a built-in Control UI page, as a browser-plugin page after plugin UI entry points land, or as a narrower host-owned manual-action surface first?
rationale: Current browser primitives exist, but the requested feature exposes authenticated browser state and defines user/agent resume semantics, so maintainers need to choose the product and security boundary before implementation.

options.title: Operator-scoped browser handoff surface
options.body: Add a narrow host-owned or browser-plugin-owned panel for status, tabs, focus/open/close, explicit takeover, and resume, with redaction and authorization rules included from the start.

options.title: Wait for generic plugin UI entries
options.body: Defer browser-specific UI until the broader plugin Control UI entry-point contract lands and then let the browser plugin own the page under that contract.

options.title: Keep CLI and docs only
options.body: Close this feature direction and rely on browser CLI/RPC plus service-specific manual-action messages for login handoff.

recommendation.title: Operator-scoped browser handoff surface
recommendation.body: Add a narrow host-owned or browser-plugin-owned panel for status, tabs, focus/open/close, explicit takeover, and resume, with redaction and authorization rules included from the start.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to recent browser/UI source history and already made the item-specific product call that this issue is the canonical login handoff tracker.
